```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
example_root <- tempfile("cttir-audit-")
dir.create(example_root)
old_options <- options(cttiR.catalog_dir = file.path(example_root, "catalog"),
  cttiR.runtime_dir = file.path(example_root, "runtime"))
```

## doctor(), audit() and update() do different things

| Function | Purpose | Side effects |
|---|---|---|
| `doctor()` | brief read-only diagnostics | none |
| `audit()` | full check registry, reports, optional allowlisted repairs | reports only when `output` is given; repairs only with `repair = TRUE` |
| `update()` | refresh the knowledge/resource catalogs | new immutable snapshots and one pointer change; never installs packages |

```{r audit}
p <- cttiR::project("Audit example", "methods", "Describe a tabular comparison", path = example_root)
report <- cttiR::audit(p$path)
report
head(as.data.frame(report)[, c("id", "status", "message")], 10)
```

The default audit reads metadata only. It never opens referenced datasets,
runs study pipelines, installs dependencies, starts services or contacts a
network. The `integration` scope opts into temporary synthetic projects and an
isolated catalog fixture; `live = TRUE` additionally allows a bounded probe of an
already running owned local model.

`RES-008` compares every required and optional dependency pin with installed
version metadata, including CRAN interoperability packages. In renv mode it reads
the project library; a matching global installation does not substitute for a
missing project package. Unresolved pins warn for a scaffold and fail an
`analysis_ready` claim. Matching version numbers alone do not establish matching
source hashes or scientific suitability. Nothing is installed by this check.

Generated interoperability helpers also enforce pins at runtime. Run them from
the project root so they can read `cttir-lock.json`, or pass a complete reviewed
`pins` list explicitly. They refuse a missing lock, missing package pins and
installed-version mismatches, including when the class namespace is already
loaded. The lock is read as JSON; no project code is sourced, and nothing is
installed automatically. `jsonlite` reads the lock and its version is then
checked against that lock before object operations proceed.

Repairs are an explicit allowlist: restore a missing managed file whose
baseline is known, roll back an interrupted write whose writer has stopped, and
repoint a corrupt catalog pointer to the last verified snapshot. Edited files
are never overwritten.

```{r repair}
unlink(file.path(p$path, "code", "validate_project.R"))
cttiR::audit(p$path, scope = "project")$overall_status
repaired <- cttiR::audit(p$path, scope = "project", repair = TRUE)
repaired$overall_status
file.exists(file.path(p$path, "code", "validate_project.R"))
```

`audit(strict = TRUE)` raises `cttir_audit_failed` after writing any requested
reports when a required check fails or stays unverified; the condition carries
the full report for CI use.

## Readiness levels

Project creation always reports `scaffold_ready`. Higher levels come from local
evidence: matching installed or renv-locked dependency versions
(`environment_ready`), a passing synthetic demonstration produced by the
unmodified stage code (`demo_verified`), a passing study-data run receipt
(`data_ready`) and, finally, recorded mappings, reviewed settings, analysis
approval and approved stage adapters (`analysis_ready`). None of these is a
scientific validation of results.

## Local runtime and planner

The opt-in live audit (`INT-003`) checks both structured output and a fixed
synthetic linear-regression planning task. It requires an accepted local proposal,
the expected grounded capability and current bundled workflow approval evidence.
It can diagnose an unqualified model without promoting it. These probes use no
project goal or study data and are not an independent usefulness benchmark.
The audit budget accommodates the initial probe and at most two planner requests
under the supported timeout settings.

`setup()` prepares an owned, cloud-disabled Ollama runtime on Linux x86_64 from
a pinned publisher archive and verifies a local model with a bounded structured
probe. A dry run is read-only:

```{r setup-plan}
plan <- cttiR::setup(dry_run = TRUE)
plan$state
plan$model$name
```

The default project planner is deterministic. The recorded 7B CPU results are
currently development evidence only. Fresh independent qualification on the
shipped artifact remains pending, so no manifest model authorizes automatic
planning. Automatic model selection retains its tested resource policy, but
blocks acquisition when no independently qualified model is available.
With `options(cttiR.planner = "local_llm")`
and a verified owned runtime, a model plans only if the manifest marks it
qualified at its exact digest and the tested prompt, grounding policy, registry,
schema, runtime binary and inference settings still match; otherwise the deterministic planner is used and
the fallback reason `model_not_qualified` is recorded. Using an unqualified
model needs the separate acknowledgement
`options(cttiR.planner_allow_unqualified = TRUE)`, and its qualification label
is then stored with every decision it made. Goals that read like instructions
to the model are never sent (`goal_injection_suspected`). Deterministic planning
and `ask()` block hard instruction markers; ambiguous phrases such as "safety
mode" retain keyword matching with a review note. Screened goals cannot add
keyword-derived workflow candidates. Explicit options
always win over suggestions, and replay or `sync()` never re-plan.

The prompt includes registered package names and aliases. A validated model
proposal retains only capabilities with registered keyword evidence in the goal;
omissions are recorded in bounded notes and the project decision evidence.
This can omit legitimate requests expressed without those keywords. Filtering
is not workflow approval, and fixed inference settings do not guarantee identical
suggestions. Review proposed study decisions before using them for analysis.
Requests matching more capabilities than the proposal schema permits return no
capability selection and ask for a narrower request. Candidate capability IDs
carry an explicit unapproved-status note; they do not become reviewed adapters.

Planner and assistance qualification also bind package function bodies, defaults,
static rules, R/platform and direct/transitive Imports and Depends versions.
Mutable caches are excluded. The implementation fingerprint is deliberately
conservative: even an unrelated package-code change reopens qualification.
These identity checks do not prove scientific validity or the integrity of a
third-party package rebuilt with different contents under the same version.
Long inputs are bounded again after JSON escaping, preserving valid input JSON.
Planner 4 keeps the longest prefix that fits this character budget. Every reply,
including a repair, must report a valid prompt token count with room for the
reserved output tokens in the configured context. Missing or excessive counts
cause `context_overflow` fallback without another request. This checks the
runtime's reported count; it is not an independent tokenizer or proof that the
runtime preserved every input token. Earlier planner evaluations remain
historical development evidence and do not qualify the new policy.

Planner benchmark reports separate post-grounding scores from the capability
claims present before keyword filtering, and retain the removed IDs in exported
rows. With diagnostic `keep_raw = TRUE`, parseable raw capability arrays are
also scored against the case's gold capabilities, including rejected attempts.
Missing, malformed or truncated raw replies remain unscored; the report gives
the number of scored attempts so absent diagnostics cannot masquerade as a
zero unsupported-claim rate. The first-attempt rejection rate excludes cases
where no model request was made. These additional diagnostics do not replace
or relax any pre-registered threshold. Historical comparison results and
representative failures are bundled in `benchmarks/planner-review-history.json`;
the old compact reports cannot recover all pre-grounding claims.

Accepted local planning stores the model identity, digest, qualification, prompt
version and request options in the specification and project lock. Replay uses
these recorded values; older specifications with no recorded settings keep them
unknown. `cttiR.planner_threads` defaults to the smaller of 16 and the measured
physical core count. `cttiR.planner_processor` defaults to `"cpu"`; `"auto"`
permits unqualified GPU use. `cttiR.planner_timeout` defaults to 120 seconds
(allowed range 5 to 600). Changing options does not confer qualification.
Historical CPU results used a Xeon w9-3475X with 16 threads; other CPUs and
runtime backends have not inherited that measured result.

## Data flow and privacy

* Goals, configuration files, documentation and model output are treated as
  untrusted data; nothing is evaluated.
* Study data are never read during creation, synchronization, audit or catalog
  updates. `check_analysis_data()` and `code/run_workflow.R` read data only when
  you supply or bind them explicitly.
* Machine-specific paths belong in the ignored `.cttir/local.yml`.
* The planner (when enabled) and `ask()` never send text off the machine; the
  runtime listens on loopback only and refuses cloud-backed models.
* Exported Shiny drafts can contain your text; review them before sharing.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Next step |
|---|---|
| `cttir_transaction_conflict` with an active writer | wait for the other operation; if it crashed, run `cttiR::audit(path, repair = TRUE)` |
| `cttir_catalog_corrupt` | `cttiR::audit(scope = "knowledge", repair = TRUE)` or `cttiR::rollback_knowledge(<id>, dry_run = FALSE)` |
| `workflow_approval_pending` blocker | the pinned catalog lacks approvals for a stage; review with `cttiR::packages(path)` |
| `environment_pending` blocker | install the pinned versions or enable `workflow$environment = "renv"` with `prepare_environment = TRUE` |
| `code/run_workflow.R` stops with a list | record the listed mappings/settings/approval with `cttiR::sync()` and bind the dataset in `.cttir/local.yml` |
| `setup()` returns `blocked` | read `$blockers`; offline mode never downloads, and only Linux x86_64 is supported |

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
options(old_options)
unlink(example_root, recursive = TRUE)
```


Setup previews (`setup(dry_run = TRUE)`) report offline-known acquisition and
planning blockers separately, published full download sizes, available disk
space and recorded disk admission budgets. Sizes are not estimates of remaining
incremental downloads, and an absent model profile has unknown size/budget.
A verified owned process is reported with PID and host; file presence alone does
not verify a runtime. Project summaries report the planning mode used and direct
users to this preview without probing or starting an optional local runtime.
Explicit model preparation remains available for diagnostics even when the
model is unqualified; it does not grant planning qualification.

## Installing an exact model release

`setup_release()` takes a locally reviewed JSON manifest and its SHA-256 from a
separately trusted release record. This development package does not yet bundle a
qualified release manifest. The schema binds package, catalog, policy, prompt,
runtime, base model, adapter, GGUF and template identities. A manifest cannot grant
qualification. Linux x86_64 is the only supported acquisition platform.

```{r exact-release, eval=FALSE}
# Obtain these files and the manifest checksum from a reviewed release record.
preview <- cttiR::setup_release(
  manifest = "release.json", manifest_sha256 = trusted_manifest_sha256,
  model_file = "model.gguf", offline = TRUE
)
preview$storage
preview$download_estimate
preview$blockers

# A separate explicit action permits the previewed work.
installed <- cttiR::setup_release(
  manifest = "release.json", manifest_sha256 = trusted_manifest_sha256,
  model_file = "model.gguf", offline = TRUE,
  dry_run = FALSE, consent = TRUE
)
```

Preview makes no HTTP requests or writes. It reports conservative disk admission
requirements, including staging space; these are estimates, not reservations.
Offline import still needs the pinned runtime to be installed already. Omitting
`model_file` permits a verified cache or, with downloads enabled, the immutable
HTTPS model URL in the manifest. Model and runtime transfers require command-line
`curl` and resume retained partial downloads. Corrupt
or conflicting files remain for inspection. An occupied unmanaged daemon is not
modified. Select an unused loopback port through `cttiR.ollama_endpoint` when an
isolated runtime is needed. The Runtime view exposes the same release inputs and
consent control.

The installer checks the local model digest and template and performs a bounded
structured-output probe. `model_ready` is separate from assistance qualification,
project environment readiness and analysis approval. Keep previous release
manifests and artifacts for rollback by explicitly selecting their original
manifest. The atomic runtime-state record identifies the activated release.

## Storage and process lifetime

```{r managed-storage, eval=FALSE}
cttiR::runtime_storage()

# Choose exact download basenames from the inventory; nothing is auto-selected.
cleanup <- cttiR::runtime_cleanup(files = selected_download_basenames)
cttiR::runtime_cleanup(files = selected_download_basenames,
  expected = cleanup$expected, dry_run = FALSE, consent = TRUE)

shutdown <- cttiR::runtime_stop()
cttiR::runtime_stop(expected = shutdown$expected,
  dry_run = FALSE, consent = TRUE)
```

Storage inventory covers model downloads, runtime archives, blobs and retained manifests, excluding
runtime libraries and logs from its byte total. Cleanup protects all retained
release pins, model blobs and unrelated files. It rechecks selected hashes under
the setup lock and records removals. Shutdown rechecks process ownership and
creation time, sends a graceful signal only to that process and preserves all
files. A `stopping` result reports that the process remained alive after five
seconds; it does not claim that all resources were released. No package hook
starts, stops or downloads a runtime or model.
